description: State machine transitions should be tested for both valid and invalid paths.

Flag actual business-logic changes without updated or added tests: server-side invariants, permissions, state transitions, money or availability rules, API or worker behavior, data transformations, or contract semantics. SKIP purely presentational UI variants, class composition, visual-only branches, AND pure wrappers around a single external dependency where any unit test would only mock that dependency (these fail the value gate). Load the project's testing-conventions skill, if one exists, before flagging — apply its value gate first.
Flag new reusable UI component variants or presentational branches without focused tests when a regression would be user-visible. Do not use this rule for one-off markup or class-only changes.
Unit test where mock returns X and assertion checks X came back with no transformation or branching in between. Proves the mock works, not the code.
N near-identical tests varying only the field name when all fields go through the same code path. Collapse into one test with multiple assertions.
Mock setup exceeds 5x the assertion code. Replace with an integration/e2e test.
No shared mutable state between tests - each test sets up and tears down its own data.
Tests must not depend on execution order.
Flag test files that import or mutate module-level variables shared across test cases.
Flag tests that assert on internal method call counts instead of observable results.
Flag tests where the assertion cannot possibly fail given the test setup.
Mock at boundaries (DB adapters, HTTP clients, queue producers), not internal service methods.
Flag mocks that replicate business logic instead of returning fixed responses.

Run `wc -l` on EVERY new or modified test file in the diff, not just the ones another finding already implicates — a large PR that splits one oversized file can still leave sibling new files over the cap unflagged. Per the project's testing-conventions skill, if one exists (otherwise use these defaults): <=150 lines is fine, 151-300 needs a look, and >300 MUST be split or have helpers extracted before merging. Applies only to new/modified files; do not flag a pre-existing oversized file the PR didn't touch.
